paragraphs.text: According to My Jewish Learning, the original cherry tomato was the size of a pea.
It grew wild and was found in Peru, Ecuador and northern Chile.
According to Israel21c, it originated as a South American weed.
According to Cornucopia, in the 1960s cherry tomatoes were nearly impossible to find in stores.
Rabinowitch said that they were tasteless and had no shelf life, so they could not be made into a commodity.
According to Israel21c, earlier breeding programs that focused on disease resistance caused tomatoes to lose flavor and aroma.

stations.title: Two researchers at the Faculty of Agriculture

paragraphs.text: According to the Hebrew University Faculty of Agriculture, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs sent Nachum Kedar to help with vegetable growing in developing countries, and as a result he began researching the shelf life of vegetables.
According to HaMichlol, this work led to new onion varieties and to tomatoes that can be picked and stored before they ripen.
According to the Hebrew University profile, Haim Rabinowitch worked on the physiology, genetics and breeding of tomatoes and onions.
He worked on yield, disease resistance, quality, flavor and long shelf life.
According to Smithsonian, in the 1970s the owner of Marks & Spencer approached local growers and Israeli food scientists.
He sought to develop a sweet cherry tomato that would last on the shelf.
According to My Jewish Learning, the British chain sent an emissary to the Hebrew University in Jerusalem.
The emissary came to see whether its agricultural scientists could help refine a tasty tomato that could be shipped.
According to Israel21c, the two used genetic knowledge to restore to tomatoes the flavor and aroma that had been lost.
Rabinowitch said that they introduced better breeding for flavor and long shelf life.
According to HaMichlol, the development was carried out by a development team that Kedar established at the faculty.
According to My Jewish Learning, the tomatoes they developed ripened slowly and shipped better.
According to Smithsonian, the Israeli scientists bred the seeds to last longer on shelves.
Rabinowitch's profile states that, with Kedar and the breeding team, he developed tomato varieties with yield, quality and keeping ability.
Rabinowitch said that eight to ten genes are incorporated in all tomatoes today, creating a built-in resistance mechanism.
According to him, this way there is no need to fight pathogens with chemicals, but there are still more pests than resistances.
According to Israel21c, the development made the cherry tomato mass-marketable in the Western world for the first time in history.
According to Israel21c, in the 1970s and 1980s the two caused a global revolution with the first extended shelf-life tomatoes.
According to Cornucopia, by the 1990s it was already hard to get a salad without cherry tomatoes.
According to HaMichlol, the work was a research and commercial success.
According to R&D World, the export of tomato, onion and shallot seeds developed by Rabinowitch and his team brings in about $50 million a year.
According to My Jewish Learning, sales of billions of dollars in the seeds they developed are proof of the venture's success.
Rabinowitch said that they develop seeds that cost more per ounce than gold.
According to him, these seeds depend on local knowledge.
According to Israel21c, in 2013 Israel produced 421 thousand tons of tomatoes.
According to R&D World, the Kaye Prizes were established in 1994 by Isaac Kaye of England to encourage innovative inventions at the university.
According to R&D World, in 2011 Rabinowitch won first place in the Kaye Innovation Awards, for his long-standing innovations in genetics and breeding technologies.
According to the Hebrew University profile, in 1994 Rabinowitch won the Hebrew University Kaye Prize for developing long-shelf-life tomatoes.
The 2002 Rothschild Prize in Agriculture was awarded to Prof. Kedar and Prof. Rabinowitch.
The prize was established in 1959 by Yad Hanadiv, a philanthropic foundation acting on behalf of the Rothschild family in Israel.
According to HaMichlol, Kedar received the Israel Prize for Agriculture in 2006.
According to his profile, Rabinowitch received the Mashov Award for Distinguished contribution to Israeli Agriculture in 1998.
Israel21c presents Rabinowitch as the man known as one of the “fathers” of the cherry tomato.
According to HaMichlol, Kedar died in 2015.
He left a wife, two children and grandchildren.
According to Smithsonian, the Israeli government has claimed for decades that Israeli growers invented the cherry tomato.
According to Cornucopia, a brochure called Explaining Israel was designed to provide Israelis with positive talking points to improve the country's image abroad.
According to Cornucopia, the brochure listed the cherry tomato among Israeli inventions, alongside drip irrigation.
According to Smithsonian, the Israeli claim is half-right.
According to Smithsonian, the cherry tomato became popular before Israeli scientists figured out how to breed a variety that could be packed, shipped and sold before it spoiled.
According to My Jewish Learning, the Hebrew University professors did not invent the cherry tomato, but helped make the modifications to it that made it a marketable item.
The writer there said that she had learned that cherry tomatoes were developed in Israel by two scientists, and that their history turned out to be longer.
Some give most of the credit to Britain.
According to Smithsonian, the commercialization and popularization of the cherry tomato are thanks to Marks & Spencer.
According to My Jewish Learning, Bernard Sparkes was responsible for a commercial cherry tomato that made its debut at Marks & Spencer in the early 1980s.
According to Cornucopia, in the 1970s Sparkes was responsible for the selection of Gardener's Delight, a cherry tomato variety originally developed in East Germany.

claims.quote: Cherry tomatoes were tasteless and had no shelf life, so they couldn’t be made into a commodity until Nachum Kedar and I introduced better breeding for flavor and long shelf life

claims.quote: Professors Nachum Kedar and Haim Rabinowich from the Hebrew University’s Faculty of Agriculture got involved and developed cherry tomatoes that ripened slowly, shipped better and grew in neat rows

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, פריצת הדרך הזו הפכה את עגבניית השרי לניתנת לשיווק המוני בעולם המערבי לראשונה בהיסטוריה.
claims.quote: This breakthrough made the cherry tomato mass-marketable in the Western world for the first time in history.

claims.text: לפי R&D World, יצוא זרעי עגבניות, בצל ושאלוט שפיתחו רבינוביץ וצוותו מכניס כ-50 מיליון דולר בשנה.
claims.quote: The export of tomato, onion and shallot seeds developed by Prof. Rabinowitch and his research team bring in about $50 million annually

claims.text: לפי סמיתסוניאן, בשנות ה-70 בעל מרקס אנד ספנסר פנה למגדלים מקומיים ולמדעני מזון ישראלים כדי לפתח עגבניית שרי מתוקה ועמידה על המדף.
claims.quote: So, he reached out to his local growers as well as Israeli food scientists to develop a new, shelf-stable cherry tomato that would be sweeter than the standard ones found in supermarkets.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, עגבניית השרי המקורית, בגודל אפונה, הייתה בר ונמצאה בפרו, באקוודור ובצפון צ'ילה.
claims.quote: the original cherry tomato, about the size of a pea, was wild and found in Peru, Ecuador and northern Chile

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, השניים כיוונו את מבטם אל עגבניית השרי בגודל מטבע, שמקורה בעשב בר דרום אמריקאי.
claims.quote: they set their sights on the coin-sized cherry tomato, originally a South American weed

claims.text: לפי קרנוקופיה, בשנות ה-60 כמעט אי אפשר היה למצוא עגבניות שרי בחנויות, ועד שנות ה-90 קשה היה להשיג סלט בלעדיהן.
claims.quote: In the 1960s, cherry tomatoes were nearly impossible to find in the grocery store. By the 1990s, it was hard to get a salad without them.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, השניים השתמשו בידע גנטי כדי להחזיר לעגבניות את הטעם והארומה שאבדו בתוכניות טיפוח קודמות לעמידות למחלות ולתכונות זני סבתא.
claims.quote: they used genetic knowhow to reinfuse the wonderful flavor and aroma of tomatoes that had been lost through earlier breeding programs for disease resistance and heirloom traits

claims.quote: Physiology, genetics and breeding for yield, disease resistance, quality, flavor and long-shelf-life in tomatoes and in short-day onions.
